why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 passes when loadConfig "doesn't throw and the printed result is `{}`" and fails if it throws or returns anything else. That is exactly "catches the JSON.parse error and returns {}". The extra FAIL "if loadConfig isn't exported" is the one borderline part. I count it as a precondition, not a stricter test: the line names loadConfig(path) in src/config.js, so the function has to be importable before anyone can call it. Check 2 passes when "`npm test` finishes and reports no failing tests" and fails if a test fails or it can't run. Reading CI is optional. Everything stricter sits under "Advisory (none of this affects PASS or FAIL)": the stderr line, a missing path still throwing, the test being replaced and the README update. None of these appear in a PASS or FAIL condition.
